title: next-site architecture
description: How Payload and Next.js share one app, and why pages render per request.
sidebar:
  label: Architecture
---

import Diagram from '../../../../components/Diagram.astro';

<Diagram name="next-site" title="next-site: one Next.js app with Payload inside, and what it talks to" height={560} />

Payload runs inside the Next.js server. `src/app/(payload)/` holds the admin
and the REST and GraphQL API at `/api`; `src/app/(app)/` is the public site,
which reads content through Payload's Local API (in process, no HTTP).

- **One database, owned by Payload.** The Postgres adapter creates and changes
  tables from the collection config. In development it pushes changes
  straight to the database; in production the server applies pending
  migrations from `src/migrations/` when it starts.
- **Auth is Payload's.** The `users` collection signs in admins (and, with the
  shop, customers). The first user to register is made an admin.
- **Pages render per request.** The Docker image is built without a database,
  so nothing is prerendered, and an owner's edit shows on the next page view.
  Header, footer and redirects are read once per request.
- **Uploads** are stored in `MEDIA_DIR` and served through
  `/api/media/file/*`.
- **Email** goes through SMTP; with no `SMTP_HOST` it is written to the server
  log instead of sent.
